name: Atelier Form
description: A photographic textile collection proposal with architectural spacing.

slides.title:
Spaces with
softness
items: Material, craft and a focused launch plan.

slides.title: A collection built for everyday use
items: Tightly woven seat cloth forms the core range. Reinforced edges protect the areas handled most often during normal daily use.
Clay, oat and aubergine connect the collection across cushions, runners and upholstery. Texture provides variation within a deliberately limited colour range.
Standard widths and documented weave settings make the range easier to replenish. Each sample carries its yarn reference and finishing record.

slides.title: Three products, one material story
items: A compact weave gives the upholstery a firm handle. The proposed range uses two neutral grounds with one contrasting accent thread.
A lighter construction allows the runner to fold easily. Narrow edge detailing creates interest without competing with dishes and table settings.
A raised surface adds depth to the smallest format. Removable covers and consistent dimensions make this the most accessible entry product.

slides.title: Material choices shape the range
items: The proposed linen blend gives the runner a crisp surface and visible yarn variation. Reserve this construction for lightly handled pieces.
The cotton base produces a softer feel and more consistent colour. Use it for covers that customers will wash more frequently.
Choose the yarn against its intended use, then compare finished samples under daylight. Record shrinkage before confirming the final cutting dimensions.

slides.title: From yarn to finished sample
items: Confirm yarn availability and request matching lots. Keep one untouched reference skein so later deliveries can be compared against the original colour.
Produce a small sample of each construction before committing to yardage. Record tension and thread count alongside the loom setup photograph.
Wash, dry and press the samples using the proposed care instructions. Measure the finished pieces before approving them for customer presentation.

slides.title: Quality is visible in the details
items: Inspect the full length of each edge for loops and uneven tension. Reject sections that catch a finger during a light pass.
View every sample from the front and reverse under the same light. Mark unexpected floats and separate intentional variation from construction faults.
Compare the finished sample with its approved reference before packing. Keep dated records so a replacement order can reproduce the same result.

slides.title: A focused launch assortment
items: Start with three product formats so the team can explain the collection clearly and manage samples without creating an oversized assortment.
Offer six colour combinations across the initial range. Repeat the strongest neutral grounds to create a recognisable relationship between different products.
Prepare twelve finished samples for buyer meetings. Include both front and reverse views so the construction can be assessed in the room.

slides.title: How the collection reaches buyers
items: Show complete pieces beside small construction samples. Let buyers handle the material and compare finishes before discussing quantities and available delivery windows.
Provide a compact display pack with clear product dimensions. Keep the opening order simple and offer replacement samples when the display becomes worn.
Use close photographs and consistent care information on each product page. Answer practical questions about fit, cleaning and replenishment before taking an order.

slides.title: Resolve production risks early
items: A delayed yarn lot could interrupt the range. Identify an acceptable substitute during sampling and confirm the colour difference before approving any change.
Different washing conditions can alter the final size. Agree the finishing process in writing and measure every first batch against the approved sample.
Too many bespoke combinations can slow delivery. Keep the opening range focused and review custom requests after the standard products are established.

slides.title: A twelve-week release plan
items: Complete material selection and sample development. Approve the three constructions, document their finishing settings and confirm which colour combinations enter the first release.
Produce the buyer sample set and prepare product photography. Check dimensions, care information and order details against the actual finished pieces.
Present the range to selected buyers and collect structured feedback. Confirm the first production order after reviewing demand and supplier delivery windows.

slides.title: Approve the range and begin sampling
items: Approve three product formats and the proposed six colour combinations. Keep the first release small enough to support consistent finishing and replenishment.
Release the sample budget after yarn availability is confirmed. Track material usage and finishing time to establish a reliable basis for production pricing.
Meet again with finished samples, documented care results and buyer feedback. Use that evidence to confirm the opening order and launch date.
